# Read findings: unit U1 of the-box-clock-counts-only-the-goals-own-work (round 1)

Subject: candidate diff `/Users/wido/.metasystem/unit/20261109t020838-ef04a07275/round-1/worktree.diff`, SHA-256 3c7cf92ace57866ffa6a8f614f017807da64d8a64fb74db892e8ead680f30670 (checked), identical to `read.diff`, against base 4b1ec85607b0f459d0fa40f6e9acaa8c389bb8e5. The worktree's tracked and untracked changes match the candidate line for line. HEAD is the base. Exactly eight files differ: five production files and three new test files.

Judged against the build brief `/Users/wido/.metasystem/unit/.inputs/5649b89eeb3e9ce7de24b266d704dd8b/build-brief.md`, design D10/D11 and T1 on the design page.

## AGREE

No material findings.

## Checklist 1: the diff against the brief

- **budget.go, what the projection knows.** `unitRunsExecuted` is private and is initialised next to `unitAttempts`. `ElapsedOverrunMinutes` and `ElapsedOverrunRun` carry `json:"-"` (S4).
  - The new block sits after the unit-identity refusal and after the loop's consumes/authorizes/episode/`ReservationConsumesBudget` filters (S2).
  - A terminal reservation's `unitExecuted` is still type-checked first and can still refuse `BUDGET_UNKNOWN`. It now feeds `reservationExecuted` instead of a second loose read.
  - A non-terminal reservation uses the loop's `executed` (running, or a non-empty `startedAt`), as S1 requires.
  - The old `unitExecuted == false` skip is kept as `TerminalStatus && !reservationExecuted → continue`, after the set and the overrun read. That is behaviour-equivalent for attempt and minute accounting.
  - The overrun is read with `numInt`. The `> 0` guard is implied by "larger than the current value", which starts at 0, and it also keeps the `uint64` conversion safe.
- **unit_launch.go, the waiver.** `slices.DeleteFunc` removes only `Field == "elapsedLimit"`. That covers both the closed entry from `budgetAdmissionBreaches` and the breach entry from `finishBudgetProjection`.
  - The waiver is applied only when `projection.unitRunsExecuted[run]` is set.
  - The proposed-minutes breach is appended after the waiver. Attempt, minutes, active-job and `StopFence` refusals are unchanged.
  - `elapsedOverrunMin` is written only on a new reservation (a joined one returns first) and only when an entry was actually removed. It is floored to whole minutes and clamped at 0 (S5).
  - `ReconcileUnitLaunch` mutates the record in place, so the field survives collection. T2 confirms this on the check record after collection.
- **The words.** `OverrunWords` returns empty when `ElapsedOverrunRun` or `ElapsedState` is empty (S3). The format is exactly "past its box by %dm for run %s".
- **The two display sites.** Both are added right after the `PersonWords` calls: `intentBudgetView.lines` and `goalShown.budgetSection`.
- **Scope.** Nothing else changed: no change to admission.go, stop.go, `ReconcileUnitLaunch`, elapsed computation, ratchets, floors, testing.json or goldens. There are no new source comments.
  - Size: 38 production lines added and 4 removed, against an estimate of 32. That is under the 250-line stop line.

## Checklist 2: do the tests exercise the changed behaviour?

The proof command is `/usr/bin/true`, so it proves nothing, and I re-ran everything myself on this host:

- `go build ./...` and `go vet` (dispatch, cmd) passed.
- The three new tests, `TestAuditMessagesAPersonReads`, `TestAuditMessagesTraced`, `TestAuditOutputLayoutJSONUnchanged` and the neighbouring unit-retry and reserve tests all passed.
- `go test ./internal/dispatch/...` passed as a whole (exit 0).
- The brief's rule-13 cmd/metasystem prefix selection passed (exit 0).
- `./internal/steward/... ./internal/lease/... ./internal/delegation/... ./internal/launch/...` passed (all `ok`).

I ran mutations as `go test -overlay` copies, so the worktree was never touched. Each mutation failed the named test:

| Mutation | Test that failed |
|---|---|
| (a) no waiver | T1 :32; T2 :62, run held with `BUDGET_REFUSED elapsedLimit state=ADMISSION_CLOSED_ELAPSED` |
| (b) waiver for any run | T1 :73, new run R2 admitted |
| (c) waiver of attemptLimit | T1 :77 |
| (d) fence waived when the elapsed limit is waived | T1 :83 |
| (e) every reservation counted as executed | T1 :74, R3 admitted |
| (f) no `elapsedOverrunMin` | T1 :37 (zero-at-box record); T2 :73 |
| (g) words while the box is open | T3 "open" |

Three extra mutations of my own:

| Mutation | Test that failed |
|---|---|
| Overrun run id not recorded | T1 :63 |
| Each display site removed on its own | T3 at both sites; T2 :77 for the goal show site |
| Rounding up instead of floor | T1 :52, 16 instead of 15 |

T1 covers every row of the brief: admitted check with its record, projection and words; a joined check keeps its value; read and correction round 2; new run refused; unexecuted run refused; attempt limit refuses without naming `elapsedLimit`; stop fence; past box plus grace. It also covers an open-box build carrying no field and an admission exactly at the box recording 0. T2 drives the real `work build` runner and `unitLaunchAuthority` (`ReserveUnitLaunch`) through build, check, read and collection, using one injected clock shared by the manager and `commandNow`. All new tests and subtests call `t.Parallel()`.

## Non-gating observations

1. low, not material. `internal/dispatch/record.go:80-115`. `elapsedOverrunMin` is a reservation-time fact written once by `ReserveUnitLaunch`, but it is in neither `immutableFields` nor `dedicatedMetadataFields`. Its siblings are registered: `capMin`, `unitRun`, `unitRound` and `claimEpoch` are immutable, and `unitRetryAttempt` is dedicated. So a generic record patch on a pending unit reservation could add or rewrite it (record.go:647-653). The impact is display only: admission reads `unitExecuted`, `status` and `startedAt`, never this field. No caller patches it, and the brief says nothing else changes. A candidate for the later list, with `elapsedOverrunMin` going into `dedicatedMetadataFields`. RELATION: new
2. not material. T1's breach row asserts `liveStopReason(ProjectBudget(...))` instead of `FindBreachStops`. The brief permits that fallback and the builder's report says so. The diff touches neither stop.go nor the projection's breach list (the waiver filters a local slice inside `ReserveUnitLaunch`), so D11 cannot regress through this diff. RELATION: new
3. not material. T2's second-unit check asserts the worktree hold (exit 3, "the worktree belongs to run ...") instead of `BUDGET_REFUSED`. The brief allows this fallback and the builder's report says so. T1 row 3 covers the new-run refusal, and mutation (b) confirmed it fails. RELATION: new
4. Environment, not about the diff. While `go test ./internal/dispatch/...` and the cmd selection ran, files I had written in this findings directory were deleted repeatedly: logs, the mutation directory and a pid file. The directory carries a `.metasystem-store` marker. The exit codes, appended afterwards, survived, and all were 0. This file was written after every run had ended.

## Not independently re-run

I ran no grep-selected cmd/metasystem pinning test that falls outside the rule-13 prefix selection. The builder's `pinning-cmd-metasystem` artifact reports a pass. Every other checklist item was checked within the budget.

VERDICT: land
